class.name: PhysXBurnable3D
class.brief_description: Makes a wooden object (a crate, a log, debris) catch fire, burn down to glowing char and throw embers.
class.description: Add it as a child of the object to burn, or point [member target] at it; it reads the object's meshes for its size and look. The object heats up from a [PhysXFireSpread3D] nearby ([member fire]): flame contact where the ground under it is flaming, and radiation from the burning area around it. It catches fire when the heat it has taken in reaches the dose for a thick solid to reach [member ignition_temperature] (the flux-time product of fire safety engineering, with wood's thermal inertia), so a short touch of flame does not light it but a sustained one does. Once alight, the flaming patch grows from the ignition point at [member flame_spread], giving off [member heat_release_rate] over its area and burning [member fuel_mass] at wood's heat of combustion. The flame is drawn by an emitter in the fire's [PhysXFlow3D] (or [member flow]) sized by Heskestad's flame height. The surface chars from the ignition point with a ragged edge, a glowing band at the burning front, and alligator cracks that glow while it smoulders. Rain held on the wood slows it and puts it out, leaving it smouldering. Water from a [PhysXParticleFluid3D] (a bucket, a hose) on and around it wets it the same way: wet wood does not take the heat that would light it, a flaming surface goes out, and the embers on it and in its char drown. The water that meets the hot surface boils off as a white cloud of steam. While flaming it throws embers ([member ember_rate] per MW): small glowing particles lofted by the plume and carried by Flow's gas, which can start new fires where they land on dry ground.

method.name: add_brand
method.description: Rests glowing firebrands on it at [param position], on a surface facing [param normal]; [param glow] is how many brands, each weighed by how much of it is left (0 to 1). Brands on a top face stay where they land; those that hit a wall gather at its foot. A pile heats the wood under it (up to about 50 kW/m² for twenty brands in a strong wind) and can set it alight. [PhysXFireSpread3D] and burning [PhysXBurnable3D] brands call this when they land.

method.name: extinguish
method.description: Puts the flames out. Wood with fuel left keeps smouldering.

method.name: get_char_amount
method.description: How much of the surface is charred, from 0 to 1.

method.name: get_brand_pile_count
method.description: Glowing firebrands resting on it, weighed by how much of each is left.

method.name: get_ember_count
method.description: Sparks in the air (the short-lived glowing points; see [method get_firebrand_count] for the brands that can start fires).

method.name: get_firebrand_count
method.description: Firebrands in the air: bark and char flakes lofted by the fire's own plume and carried by the wind, which can start spot fires where they land on a [PhysXFireSpread3D]'s ground.

method.name: get_fuel_left
method.description: Kilograms of wood left to burn.

method.name: get_heat_flux
method.description: The heat reaching the object from the fire around it, in kW/m².

method.name: get_heat_release
method.description: The heat the object gives off while flaming, in kW.

method.name: get_spot_fire_count
method.description: Spot fires its firebrands have started.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Whether the object is unburnt, flaming, smouldering or burnt out.

method.name: ignite
method.description: Sets the object alight at the point of its bounds nearest [param position] (world space).

members.member: For a [PhysXDestructible3D] target: the share of its section burnt away at which it gives way. The section is lost as timber loses it in a fire (EN 1995-1-2's reduced cross-section: char at about 0.8 mm a minute and a zero-strength layer growing to 7 mm behind it, from both faces of its thinnest side), and the bonds in the burning patch weaken with it, breaking at this share, so the burning parts break off gently and what is cut loose from the ground falls. A 4 cm board wall gives way after about 7 minutes of flaming. Its char look stays on the pieces.
Sparks thrown per second for each MW of heat released (for the look; they do not light anything).

Throws sparks and firebrands while flaming: about 10 brands per kg of wood burnt, lofted by the fire's own column (Byram's plume speed for its heat release), carried by the wind and able to start spot fires where they land on dry ground fuel of a [PhysXFireSpread3D].
The [PhysXFireSpread3D] that heats the object, and where its embers land.
How fast the flaming patch grows over the surface, in m/s.
Scales the flame and smoke the object puts into Flow.
The [PhysXFlow3D] that draws the flame. Empty uses the [member fire]'s.
Kilograms of wood to burn. 0 works it out from the object's size (a third of its bounding volume, as wood).
Brightness of the burning front, the glowing cracks and the embers.
Heat given off per square metre of flaming surface, in kW/m².
Surface temperature at which the wood catches fire, in degrees Celsius.
The object that burns: its meshes give the size and take the char look.
